title: Suffices to the generalized equation for Fermat's Last Theorem n = 3
intent: Reduce Fermat's Last Theorem for exponent 3 to the generalized equation FermatLastTheoremForThreeGen over the cyclotomic integers (a stronger statement in which the unit u is free), then close that generalized statement by infinite descent on the multiplicity of λ = ζ₃ − 1 in c.

children.name: FermatLastTheoremForThree_of_FermatLastTheoremThreeGen
children.statement:
lemma FermatLastTheoremForThree_of_FermatLastTheoremThreeGen
    [NumberField K] [IsCyclotomicExtension {3} ℚ K] :
    FermatLastTheoremForThreeGen hζ → FermatLastTheoremFor 3
children.closed_by: own proof (166-178): intro H; refine fermatLastTheoremThree_of_three_dvd_only_c …, then refine H a b c 1 …; the six subgoals close by rwa / exact dvd_trans / exact IsCoprime.intCast / simpa using mod_cast

theorem exists_Solution_multiplicity_lt :
    ∃ S₁ : Solution hζ, S₁.multiplicity < S.multiplicity
children.closed_by: own proof (735-738): obtain ⟨S', hS'⟩ from exists_Solution_of_Solution' (Solution'_descent S), then exact ⟨S', hS' ▸ Solution'_descent_multiplicity_lt S⟩

applicability.goal_shape: A main theorem P (here FermatLastTheoremFor 3) is proved by first applying a backward rule P_from_Q : Q → P and then proving the stronger, more general Q (here FermatLastTheoremForThreeGen hζ, which quantifies over a free unit u and over the ring of integers 𝓞 K).
applicability.use_when: the generalized statement is genuinely stronger — extra variables or a free parameter (here the unit u) — yet still provable, and the extra freedom is exactly what lets the real argument (here descent on the multiplicity of λ) close.
applicability.avoid_when: the strengthened statement is not actually true, is no easier than the original, or the backward step Q → P needs a non-trivial transfer (here the ideal-norm argument Ideal.norm_dvd_iff in lines 172-178) that does not go through.

consequences: The move replaces the goal FermatLastTheoremFor 3 by the obligation FermatLastTheoremForThreeGen hζ (lines 755-771): the reduction lemma's premise is a stronger statement over all units u and all a, b, c in 𝓞 K. Two obligations are created: (1) the backward step Q → P must be faithful — here it needs the ideal-norm transfer Ideal.norm_dvd_iff to move a ℤ solution into 𝓞 K (lines 172-178); (2) Q must be strong enough to carry the descent, which is exactly why the unit u is left free (the descent cannot control u, module comment lines 42-46). Failure modes: strengthening too far makes Q false; strengthening too little leaves the descent without the free parameter it needs; the descent itself needs a well-founded measure (the multiplicity of λ in c) and a minimality lemma, and each step must produce a strictly smaller Solution.
